about: LUKE was founded by Thomas and Kristin Vogele with a single wine, the 2012 Cabernet Sauvignon, made to show what the Wahluke Slope can do. The wines are made at Evergreen Family Wines’ Mattawa winery, a partnership of more than a decade that became an acquisition in late 2025, with the Vogeles staying on to guide the label. The brand nods to the spirit of the American West, and its Cabernet has been a critics’ favorite at its price; the 2018 placed on Wine Enthusiast’s Top 100.

The 2021 is 95% Cabernet Sauvignon with 4% Merlot and 1% Petit Verdot, drawn from several Wahluke Slope and Columbia Valley sites including Weinbau, Ravenscliff, Southwind, Obelisco and Seven Hills. The slope’s heat and sun give ripe, dark fruit, while the river’s cooler nights keep it fresh. The wine is aged in a mix of French and American oak.

The winery’s notes mention marionberry and dark chocolate with hints of mint, then blackberry and currant touched with coffee, cedar and smoke over polished tannins. Wine Enthusiast described aromas rich enough to approach cassis, with blueberry and cinnamon on a plush, medium-acid palate and a touch of cedar on the finish.
